verdicts.note: Sitting first-term District 2 commissioner [S1] running on her term's record (balanced budget, jail compliance, reorganization, ordinances moved forward) [S1][S2], with about 30 years of county project work and 10 years on the planning commission [S1][S2]. One term is short tenure, which the medium confidence reflects, but she is the race's proven-record case against a challenger with no county office. S1 and S2 exist and support the basis. Summary and highlights match S1, S2, S3 and S6.

Pole_a evidence: the in-house reorganization that 'made us leaner' by not backfilling positions [S2], limiting hiring to crucial positions [S2], the December 2025 selective hiring freeze [S5] and a 'balanced and sustainable budget' [S1]. Her push to 'go out and find more money' (landfill diversification, timber trust lands) [S2] is about revenue, not expanding programs, so -1 rather than -2 is right. Minor: the basis says she seeks 'grants'; the dossier records new revenue from industry and timber trust management, not grants.

No elected county office; challenging the incumbent; long state service (State Parks, 30+ years law enforcement), a union executive-board seat and a community council seat [S1][S3]. Those keep him at +1, not +2. The profile facts are documented in the pamphlet and an interview, so high confidence on a profile description is acceptable. Summary and highlights match S1-S5.

Public safety as 'the number one responsibility of government', at least two more deputies, more dispatchers and jail staffing [S2][S3] are pole_a; a dedicated crisis responder and jail as 'the last thing' for people in mental-health crisis [S3] pull toward the middle. -1 medium holds. The 2024 'defund the police' statement and HB 2765 testimony [S2][S4] point the same direction; they do not justify -2 given the crisis-responder position.

Attacked toward -1: the 'REAL ... Limited' plank and protecting existing revenue [S2] are pole_a. But it is a slogan, while his concrete proposals add at least two deputies, more dispatchers and a crisis responder [S2][S3], which is added county spending. 0 as genuinely mixed is defensible; the _contest's 'both lean toward restraint' rests mainly on the slogan.

The reform axis is about money and power in politics (PAC money, term limits, dark money, RCV, direct democracy). 'Winging it' is his criticism of how the jail transition was handled, and 'You can't just do business as usual' is about unfilled county mental-health positions [S3]; both are management-process critiques, not structural political reform. The basis also adds 'new recruitment strategies', which the dossier does not say (it says he wants to find out why positions go unfilled and 'find a way to do something different'). The _contest itself lists reform as having little direct evidence.
